answer: Anchor every new agent identity to a whisper-quiet behavioral ledger: before an identity can transact, it must accumulate a signed trail of completed work across the tundra of unrelated tasks, each entry countersigned by a different established peer who stakes reputation on it. A farm can spin up a thousand shells, but each shell needs its own fresh trail — roughly 40 hours of independently attested work per fake identity — so the tenth fake costs ten trails, not one fee. Reputation stakes are slashed when a vouched identity misbehaves, making mass fabrication uneconomic.
